title: Emrys and the Weather
premise: Lior Okonkwo, a piano tuner who reads a house's grief through its radiators and pipes, returns to her late grandmother's home to settle an estate no one will discuss. A stranger named Emrys appears at the funeral calling the family by an old name — the one her grandmother renounced decades ago — claiming to be owed a goodbye that was never spoken. As Lior tunes the house's failing radiators, each one releases a memory of what her grandmother buried: a betrayal, a lost sibling, a name traded for survival. In the end, Lior speaks the old name aloud in the empty parlor, freeing both the house and herself from the inventory of unsaid things.
about_author: P. M. Amberdale is the pen name of a former piano restorer who spent fifteen years listening to old houses before turning to fiction. They write quietly devastating literary novels about inheritance, sound, and the families we invent to survive our own histories.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Returning for the funeral, Lior catalogs the house through its sounds — a radiator that hisses like her grandmother's unfinished sentences, a door that sticks where something was once hidden. At the graveside, a stranger called Emrys uses the family's abandoned name, and her aunt goes white. The beat is dislocation: home rendered suddenly foreign, and the first crack in the family's careful silence.

chapters.title: What the Radiators Remember
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Hired to prepare the house for sale, Lior tunes its heating system and discovers each radiator holds a distinct acoustic signature — and with it, fragments of memory she has no right to know: a woman's voice, a train station, a name being refused. Emrys returns, asking not for money but for acknowledgment. The beat deepens into compulsion: Lior can't stop listening, even as the family demands she stop asking.

chapters.title: The Name Nobody Uses
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, shifting mid-chapter to Emrys. Confronted by her aunt, Lior learns the truth: her grandmother had a brother, erased after he chose exile over silence during the family's darkest year. Emrys is his son, dying, seeking only to be claimed. The aunt burns letters; the radiator in the parlor bursts. The climax arrives as Lior realizes the goodbye must come from her — the only one still willing to listen.

chapters.title: Out Loud
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. With Emrys weakening in the guest room, Lior repairs the parlor radiator one final time and, as its heat rises, speaks the old name aloud — full, unashamed, into the room where it was forbidden. The house settles; the sticking door opens freely. Emrys dies at peace days later, and Lior keeps neither the house nor the silence. The resolution is release: identity chosen over inherited quiet.
